groups.title: Server State Management
groups.question: Your React app's data goes stale after edits, and every like takes a second to show. Explain how TanStack Query manages server data.

followUps.React Query for Server State: What does TanStack Query handle that manual fetching does not?
followUps.Cache Invalidation and Stale-While-Reval: How do staleTime and invalidation keep data fresh?
followUps.Optimistic Updates for Instant Feedback: How does an optimistic update work and what happens on failure?

evidence.text: It treats server data separately from UI state.
It handles caching, background refetching and loading and error states.
useQuery reads data and useMutation changes it.
staleTime is how long cached data counts as fresh.
Stale data is shown while a refetch runs in the background.
Invalidating a query after a mutation refetches the changed data.
The cache is updated immediately before the server confirms.
If the request fails, the previous value is restored.
This makes actions feel instant on slow connections.

notEnough: Only saying the UI updates first.

groups.title: Global State and Forms
groups.question: Your app passes the theme and modal state through many layers, and a long recipe form re-renders on every keystroke with hand-written validation. Explain how you would improve both.

followUps.Global State with Zustand or Context: When would you use Zustand or context for global state?
followUps.Schema Validation with Zod and React Hoo: How do React Hook Form and Zod work together?

evidence.text: UI state shared across routes, like theme or open modals, suits a small store or context.
Zustand avoids Redux boilerplate and lets components subscribe to just what they use.
Server data belongs in TanStack Query, keeping global state small.
React Hook Form uses uncontrolled inputs to avoid re-rendering on every keystroke.
Zod defines the validation rules as a schema.
A resolver connects them so the form is validated against the schema.

groups.title: Accessible UI Patterns
groups.question: Keyboard users cannot open your custom dropdown, and your modal does not trap focus. Explain how you would make these components accessible.

followUps.ARIA Roles and Keyboard Navigation: When should you add ARIA roles, and what must every interactive component support?
followUps.Accessible Component Libraries: Why use a headless library like Radix for modals and dropdowns?

evidence.text: Use semantic HTML first and add ARIA only when needed.
Every interactive component must work with the keyboard.
Focus must be visible and move in a logical order.
Headless libraries give accessible behaviour for complex components.
They handle focus management and keyboard support that are easy to get wrong.
They are unstyled, so you apply your own design.

groups.title: Advanced React Patterns
groups.question: Your React bundle is large and a filtered list re-renders slowly. Explain how you would split code and avoid unnecessary work.

followUps.Code Splitting with React.lazy and Suspe: How do React.lazy and Suspense reduce the first download?
followUps.useMemo and useCallback for Performance: When do useMemo and useCallback help, and why profile first?

evidence.text: React.lazy loads a component's code only when it is needed.
Suspense shows a fallback while it loads.
The build creates separate chunks for lazy routes.
useMemo caches an expensive computed value.
useCallback keeps a function reference stable, which helps memoized children.
Profiling first shows whether the work is actually slow, since memoization has its own cost.
